newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam port area traffic up 12.9 pct in 1st qtr.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam port area traffic up 12.9 pct in 1st qtr.

text.p: Amsterdam area port traffic grew by 12.9 percent to 14.5 million tonnes in the first quarter of 1997, the port authority said on Monday.

Dry bulk shipments increased by 11.6 percent to 9.5 million tonnes, with coal up 16 percent to more than three million tonnes. Ore traffic totalled 2.7 million tonnes, up 17.7 percent from the first quarter of 1996.

Liquid bulk shipments showed an increase of 24.6 percent to almost three million tonnes. Of this total, 2.3 million tonnes consisted of oil products, which was some 40 percent higher than in the year-ago period.
Rising oil prices had created a large demand for oil products storage capacity, the port authority added.

The Amsterdam port handled more than two million tonnes of general cargo in the first quarter of this year, 4.6 percent more than in the same period of 1996. The ro-ro sector grew by seven percent to 144,000 tonnes because of rising car sales.
The port authority said it expected 1997 to be a year of further growth, as a result of new capacity becoming available.
Last March, the Amsterdam port said its 1996 total traffic had risen by 8.8 percent to a record of 54.7 million tonnes.
